sum: Siemens Energy drew fresh support from two major brokers this week, with JPMorgan and UBS both reaffirming bullish stances just days before the company is due to report full-year results. The stock closed Friday up 3.8% at EUR 117.20, a rare bright spot on a day when the DAX fell sharply, according to dts.

JPMorgan kept its "Overweight" rating and a EUR 245 price target. Analyst Phil Buller pointed to an investor survey showing muted expectations ahead of the upcoming quarterly report and the capital markets day. UBS had already confirmed its "Buy" rating and EUR 210 target on Wednesday, with analyst Christopher Leonard arguing that the stock's losses during the sector-wide selloff were unjustified.

The rebound comes after a difficult stretch. Over the past seven days the shares are still down 7.3%. Media reports attributed the prior pressure to worries about stricter US rules for AI data centres and a generally weaker equity market mood. Siemens Energy was singled out as particularly sensitive to news on AI data centres because it supplies key customers in that industry, and the concern was that tighter regulation could hit those clients.

The Südwest Presse reported Thursday that fears over AI regulation and the broader market dragged the stock lower without any concrete negative company-specific trigger. The reports did not identify a company-specific catalyst for Friday's recovery either.

On the corporate side, Transition Industries signed a binding EPC contract with Siemens Energy and Techint Engineering & Construction on 30 October for an electrolysis plant at the Pacifico Mexinol project in Sinaloa, Mexico. The facility will have a capacity of around 210 MW. The agreement is subject to customary conditions precedent, including project financing, with construction scheduled to begin in early 2027.

Separately, Siemens Energy and Japan's METI signed a cooperation agreement on 29 October covering floating offshore wind, supply chains and workforce development. The company plans to establish its first strategic operations and maintenance base in Asia, located in Hokkaido.
Siemens Energy has scheduled the release of fourth-quarter and fiscal 2026 results for 11 November.

Siemens Q2 Results: Net profit up 4%, revenue surges 17% on infrastructure, private capex spending
sum: Robust private spending and infrastructure demand fueled a double-digit surge in revenue and a sharp jump in new order bookings for Siemens. Yet, margin pressures mounted as commodity and currency swings drove up material costs. Discover how management plans to protect profitability against ongoing supply chain volatility.

Technology firm Siemens Ltd on Friday (November 6) reported a 3.9% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹504 crore for the July-September 2026 quarter, compared with ₹485 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Revenue rose 17% to ₹5,734 crore from ₹4,900 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 2.8% year-on-year to ₹626 crore from ₹609 crore. However, the EBITDA margin contracted to 10.9% from 12.4% in the corresponding quarter last year.

Siemens reported a 37.8% year-on-year increase in new orders to ₹6,228 crore during the July-September 2026 quarter. Its order backlog grew 12% to ₹47,034 crore. Profit from operations stood at 9.5% during the quarter.

Sunil Mathur, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Siemens Limited, said, "Siemens Limited delivered strong growth in both Orders and Revenue, driven by continued Capex spending in infrastructure and an increase in private sector Capex. Profitability continues to be impacted mainly by volatility in commodity prices and foreign exchange, resulting in higher material costs."

sum: Siemens and Siemens Healthineers announced on Thursday, November 5, 2026, that the healthcare subsidiary will change its name to Healthineers as part of its planned separation from Siemens. The joint announcement gives Siemens a clearer industrial technology profile while setting a formal milestone for the proposed 2027 spin-off.

Siemens stock traded at 278.80 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:08 CET on Thursday, November 5, 1.14 percent above the Xetra close of Wednesday, November 4. The real-time quote of Siemens stock provides the latest market indication.

The proposal would make Healthineers the future name of Siemens Healthineers after deconsolidation. The company said the name change must be approved at the Siemens Healthineers annual shareholders' meeting. The planned spin-off itself is also scheduled to go before the annual shareholders' meetings of both companies in February 2027.

The legal separation will be completed when the spin-off is entered in the German Commercial Register. Only after that step is expected to come the brand migration. Siemens and Healthineers agreed a three-year transition period to support the re-registration of legal entities and products, so the change will unfold gradually rather than through an immediate switch.

Siemens CEO Roland Busch said the move reflects Healthineers' development into a global healthcare leader and sharpens Siemens' profile as a company that scales industrial AI in the real world. The statement links that strategy to Siemens' combination of physical and digital technologies across industry, infrastructure, mobility and healthcare.

For Siemens investors, the announcement separates two strategic questions. Healthineers would gain a distinct identity and shareholder structure, while Siemens would place greater emphasis on industrial businesses and applications that connect the real and digital worlds. The transaction remains subject to shareholder approval and the subsequent legal steps.

Siemens said its fiscal 2025, which ended on September 30, 2025, generated revenue of 78.9 billion euros and net income of 10.4 billion euros. The group employed around 318,000 people on a continuing-operations basis at that date.

Siemens Energy: Two Bulls, One Skeptic and a 100 € Price Target Standing Between Them
sum: Siemens Energy's stock has become a battleground where confidence in the order book collides with hard questions about what investors are already paying for it. Two bullish research houses and one determined bear have staked out positions ahead of the company's full-year 2026 results on 11 November — a date that will also bring fresh medium-term targets, reportedly extending out to 2030.

Bernstein built its recommendation on Siemens Energy's positioning in the electricity supply chain for data centres, a theme that has driven both the stock's recent swings and its recovery. The shares climbed 2.0% in a friendly session for companies seen as beneficiaries of the data centre boom, with media reports pointing to repeated buying in that cohort after an earlier pullback. Strong quarterly results from US rival GE Vernova were cited as a tailwind.

Bank of America had already reaffirmed its buy rating on 29 October, calling the share price decline overdone and pointing to encouraging signals from the figures published by GE Vernova and Hitachi Energy. The two houses agree on direction but not on emphasis: Bernstein leans on the data centre angle, while Bank of America draws on the broader sector read-across. Neither set of peer results is Siemens Energy's own — they sketch the demand backdrop, not the company's performance.

The earlier sell-off, by contrast, was attributed in media reports to a global wave of pressure on AI-related stocks following results from Amazon and Intel. Siemens Energy was caught in the downdraft; no company-specific announcement triggered the move.

mwb Research staked out the opposite corner on 22 October, reiterating its sell rating with a 100 € price target — even while expecting a strong final quarter. That combination is the crux of the disagreement. On the near-term trajectory the two camps need not contradict each other at all. The real argument is valuation: from mwb's standpoint, even solid results can fall short if the share price already discounts exceptionally high expectations.

Bank of America's optimism rests on several operational levers at once — strong margin momentum in the gas business, expectations of higher grid margins, persistently high gas first-fit orders through 2027 and untapped potential in the service business.

sum: Siemens Energy kept its buyback rolling through the final days of October, purchasing 1,337,076 of its own shares between 26 October and 1 November, according to the interim disclosure published yesterday. The latest update marks the sixth such notice since the programme began on 24 September, and it brings the cumulative total repurchased to 5,850,308 shares.

The purchases were spread across every trading day of the week and executed on multiple venues, Xetra among them, so no single block trade accounts for the reported volume. Daily average prices ranged from EUR 122.6675 to EUR 135.7774 — figures that describe the actual conditions of the transactions, not price targets or any company view on what the stock is worth.

That distinction matters for how investors read the news. A buyback notice is a hard record of a capital measure already carried out. Whether the operating outlook justifies current expectations will only emerge from the business figures and guidance.

The next milestone is 11 November 2026, when Siemens Energy will publish its annual results alongside strategic targets through 2030. The completed financial year and the longer-term trajectory will share the agenda that day.

Buybacks do not substitute for that operational reckoning. What counts for shareholders is which expectations management itself confirms — and on multi-year goals especially, analyst forecasts should not be confused with binding company commitments.

The split among analysts shows why the date carries weight: a strong quarter and an attractive valuation are not the same thing. Views on the business must be kept separate from views on the share price.

Bank of America drew encouraging signals on Thursday from results at GE Vernova and Hitachi Energy, pointing to strong gas turbine margins and anticipating higher margins in grid technology. It also flagged robust gas turbine orders stretching to 2027. No new rating or price target was reported alongside that assessment.

Siemens stock gains as Naver talks spotlight industrial AI
sum: Siemens stock traded at 268.08 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:35 CET on Monday, November 2, 0.91 percent above the Xetra close of Friday, October 30. The move came as fresh industrial AI discussions added a strategic technology angle ahead of Siemens' next corporate update.

The Herald Business reported on Monday that Siemens Group Chairman Roland Busch and Naver CEO Choi Soo-yeon held a dialogue on industrial AI at the Asia-Pacific German Business Conference in Seoul on Saturday, October 31. The talks focused on combining German engineering with Asian strengths in AI, chips and digital platforms across manufacturing, energy and mobility.

Choi said industrial AI would reach a true tipping point only when small and midsize companies and their suppliers could use it with ease. She also stressed that human oversight becomes more important as AI handles a wider range of tasks. The comments frame adoption as a supply-chain and productivity issue rather than only a software feature.

Busch said industrial AI would create its full value only when deployed safely and reliably in the field and scaled across industries. That emphasis is relevant for Siemens because the group's industrial offering combines automation, software and digital-twin capabilities with applications in physical production environments.

After the dialogue, Siemens executives visited Naver's 1784 headquarters. The companies discussed cases in which Naver's digital-twin technology has been used in industrial settings and explored ways to take those applications into global markets alongside Siemens' industrial solutions. They also considered cooperation involving robotics and robot foundation models.

The discussions build on a June memorandum of understanding between Naver Cloud and Korea Siemens to advance AI transformation in manufacturing. The planned cooperation combines Siemens industrial automation and digital-twin technology with Naver Cloud's AI and cloud infrastructure, while also targeting joint customer development and industry-specific projects.
For investors, the talks reinforce Siemens' positioning in industrial AI but do not by themselves establish additional revenue or earnings.

sum: Siemens Energy shares fell 6.1% on Friday, caught in a widening pullback from artificial intelligence names. For investors, the sell-off raises a question that has less to do with the share price than with the business behind it: can the company still justify expectations built on higher prices and wider margins, or do those forecasts now need trimming?

According to dpa-AFX, doubts about the profitability of multi-billion-dollar AI investments weighed on Siemens Energy alongside its peers. Media reports pointed to Intel's weaker quarterly outlook as an additional drag on AI-linked stocks. The decline is therefore best read as a reaction to the broader market backdrop rather than to any new guidance from Siemens Energy itself.

That distinction matters. A sector-wide loss of confidence can hit companies whose own expectations are unchanged — but it can equally expose assumptions that had gone unchallenged. The price move alone does not settle which reading applies.

The more specific pressure came from Barclays, which according to media reports warned of limited room for further price and margin increases in the energy technology sector. The scepticism is thus not confined to the scale of future data-centre spending. It extends to how much economic benefit suppliers can actually extract from it.

For Siemens Energy shareholders, demand and earnings quality are two separate things. Even if investment keeps flowing, the terms available to equipment makers remain an open question. The risk therefore lies not only in possible project cuts but in assumptions about profitability that may prove too optimistic.

Comments on pricing and margins will carry particular weight at the next set of results. Hard evidence could help separate industry-wide caution from the company's own trajectory. General confidence about demand, by contrast, would not fully answer the concern about a margin ceiling.

The company's ongoing share repurchase belongs in the same assessment. Siemens Energy reported the acquisition of 1,294,334 of its own shares in its latest interim disclosure, covering the period from 19 to 25 October. In total, 4,513,232 shares had been bought back under the programme by that point.

Rosemary Siemens shares miracle story after emergency surgery
sum: Violinist, singer, and Plum Coulee native Rosemary Siemens is praising God for what she describes as a miracle after emergency surgery threatened to keep her from performing at a concert in Winkler this week.
She shared her miracle story at a concert at P.W. Enns Concert Hall over the weekend, an event she thought she would miss because of unbearable pain.
"The week went by, and I didn't go to the doctor," said Siemens. "It was now Thanksgiving Monday, and I thought I should see the doctor to get this figured out before I leave on our trip."
She connected with her doctor and scheduled an appointment for the following day.

"I went in to see her, and she said, 'You need to go straight to the emergency room,'" said Siemens. "I went straight to the ER, and within two hours I had a CT scan and an hour later they told me we're going in for surgery tonight."
Siemens had a concert scheduled at the P.W. Enns Concert Hall on Saturday, Oct. 17.

"So this was just a few days ago on Tuesday, I said, 'Am I going to be clear to travel?' and they kind of didn't really know at that point," said Siemens, who now resides in Vancouver. "He said, 'If you're feeling good, you can go.'"

This will indicate a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 6.57% during the period 2026 to 2034.

Growth in electricity demands, utilisation of advanced technology and environmental sustainability by key market players are some of the main factors that have led to the development of the India power transformers market.

There is a growing demand for electricity in India, along with industrialization and urbanization which is encouraging the market. Moreover, government policies for improving grid reliability are encouraging investments in advance transformer technology.

Transformers & Rectifiers India is an expert producer of power, distribution, furnace, and rectifier transformers, reactors, and other transformer accessories. It caters to the fields of power generation, power transmission, power distribution, industries, and renewable energy.

With a market capitalisation of Rs. 8,370 cr, the shares of Transformers & Rectifiers India Ltd closed at Rs. 278.85 per share, up from its previous close of Rs. 276.15 per share. Siemens Stock Falls 5% Despite Record AI-Fueled Industrial Profit
sum: Siemens (SIEGY), the German industrial technology leader powering factories, buildings and critical infrastructure, delivered a blockbuster quarter, but the market still sent the stock down roughly 5.2% on Thursday. Comparable revenue climbed 7% to 20.8 billion, industrial profit surged 25% to a record 3.52 billion and industrial margin widened to an impressive 17.3%. On the surface, it looked like the kind of earnings report that normally pushes shares higher.

- Is SIEGY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The numbers under the hood were just as strong. Orders jumped 14% to a record 27.9 billion, giving Siemens a healthy 1.34 book-to-bill ratio. In other words, the company booked about 7.1 billion more business than it delivered during the quarter, building an even bigger pipeline for future revenue. Smart Infrastructure continued riding the global AI and data-center boom, while free cash flow reached 4.1 billion and net income rose 15% to 2.6 billion. Management also raised fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings guidance to 11.20-11.50 per share from 10.70-11.10, another sign that confidence remains high.

The sell-off shows investors wanted even more. Reuters noted concerns over softer order growth in parts of the Digital Industries automation business, overshadowing an otherwise exceptional quarter. The valuation picture adds another layer of caution.

GuruFocus estimates a GF Value of $120.16 versus a market price of $157.08, putting the stock roughly 30.7% above its fair value estimate. That premium tells investors are already paying up for Siemens' AI, electrification and data-center story, meaning future gains will likely depend on the company continuing to deliver flawless execution rather than simply posting another strong quarter.

Siemens Energy's US Market Debut Sets Stage for High-Stakes Earnings Showdown
sum: Siemens Energy shares have become a study in contrasts this week, with the stock swinging between a sharp rebound and lingering skepticism as investors digest the company's strategic push into the US market while bracing for a pivotal earnings report. The Munich-based energy technology giant launched trading of its American Depositary Receipts on the OTCQX platform on Wednesday, a move designed to broaden its appeal to US retail investors without the regulatory burden of a full SEC registration.

The initial reception was anything but welcoming. Shares closed at €133.12 on the first day of OTCQX trading, shedding 4.02 percent as the market shrugged off what many analysts had framed as a positive development. Yet the narrative shifted dramatically just 24 hours later, with the stock surging 9 percent to €145.10, narrowing the gap to its 200-day moving average of €145.88 to a mere 0.54 percent.

That whipsaw action reflects a deeper tension running through the stock. The shares have lost roughly a fifth of their value over the past 30 days and now sit 25.80 percent below the 52-week high of €195.54 reached in April. The relative strength index stands at 44.4, suggesting the rally has not pushed the stock into overbought territory despite the day's gains.

The rebound on Thursday drew strength from multiple sources. US competitor GE Vernova released strong results that lifted the entire clean-energy complex, while Nordex surprised the market with rapid operational improvements and RWE raised its guidance. Siemens Energy also secured a major contract alongside Neptun Smulders for the North Sea Connector 2 project, a 2-gigawatt converter platform order that guarantees capacity utilization well into the next decade.
But the most consequential date on the calendar is August 5, when Siemens Energy reports third-quarter results. The earnings release will test two competing narratives about the company's trajectory.

On the bullish side, the order book has never been fuller. Beyond the North Sea Connector 2, the company recently landed a multibillion-euro contract for the Misfah and Duqm power plant projects in Oman with 2.6 gigawatts of capacity.

That is exactly what the Undervalued Stocks Based On Cash Flows screener is built to find. It focuses on companies that SWS DCF analysis views as undervalued on a cash flow basis, which can appeal if you want value exposure without making a call on any single sector. This article highlights three stocks from the screener that stand out on those cash flow and valuation grounds.

Overview: Siemens Energy is a global energy technology company that supplies gas and steam turbines, grid equipment, wind turbines and long term service and digital solutions that help utilities, industry and infrastructure customers generate, transport and store electricity.

Operations: Siemens Energy generates most of its revenue from Gas Services (€12.8b), Grid Technologies (€12.1b) and Siemens Gamesa wind (€10.1b), with additional contributions from Transformation of Industry (€5.7b) and broad geographic exposure led by Europe, C.I.S., Africa and Middle East excluding Germany (€13.2b), the United States (€10.4b) and Germany (€9.6b).

Siemens Energy is attracting attention because it links recent earnings momentum with exposure to long running themes such as electrification, data center power demand and the energy transition. Revenue and earnings growth have been very large recently, and forecasts point to double digit growth with improving profit margins and a high forecast return on equity. At the same time, analysts see the stock trading below their fair value estimates, although the wide spread in price targets shows that views are divided. The turnaround of the Siemens Gamesa wind segment and the reliance on external borrowing remain key risks. If those issues are managed well, the combination of a large order book and the company’s earnings profile could be significant for long term investors.

FuelCell Energy Shares Surge After Strategic Collaboration With Siemens (FCEL)
sum: FuelCell Energy and Siemens Partner on Large-Scale Power Solutions

FuelCell Energy (NASDAQ:FCEL) shares jumped 11% on Thursday morning after the company announced a strategic collaboration with Siemens to develop scalable fuel cell power solutions for distributed energy projects.

The partnership has been formalized through a memorandum of understanding that combines Siemens' electrical engineering expertise with FuelCell Energy's fuel cell technology to accelerate the deployment of commercial energy systems.
Under the agreement, Siemens will design and supply electrical balance of plant systems for fuel cell installations, helping support the rollout of commercial projects exceeding 100 megawatts.

The companies plan to work together across project engineering, systems integration and delivery, focusing on distributed energy solutions that combine fuel cells, battery energy storage, microgrid controls and medium-voltage electrical infrastructure.
The partnership will assess opportunities to scale these technologies while improving deployment timelines, lowering project costs and expanding commercial adoption.
FuelCell Energy develops, manufactures, operates and services fuel cell power plants used by data centres, industrial customers, utilities and other distributed generation operators.

sum: The narrative around Siemens Energy has shifted dramatically. For years, the company was defined by the troubles at its wind turbine subsidiary Gamesa. Now, with the Indian business posting explosive growth and the wind division finally back in the black, the conversation has moved from crisis management to strategic ambition — just as a key board meeting looms.

The numbers out of India are striking. In the quarter ending June 2026, the Indian subsidiary reported a 39.3 percent jump in revenue, while net profit surged 67.8 percent. The operating margin of 23.6 percent is particularly telling — it suggests Siemens Energy isn't just growing in the region, it's also wielding real pricing power. Order backlog there expanded by 16.4 percent.

The demand driver isn't hard to identify. AI data centers are consuming electricity at an unprecedented rate, and India's electrification push is accelerating in tandem. Together, these forces are filling Siemens Energy's order books at a pace that seemed unthinkable just two years ago.

Group-wide, the third quarter of fiscal 2026 delivered revenue of EUR 11.45 billion, up 17.47 percent year over year, with net profit landing at roughly EUR 1.19 billion. The standout detail: Siemens Gamesa posted an operating profit of EUR 56 million — the first positive quarterly result from the wind unit since 2022.

The order backlog climbed to a record EUR 162 billion, and management reaffirmed its full-year guidance, signaling an earnings margin before special items at the upper end of the 10 to 12 percent range.

These results land in a week that could reshape the company's future. Media reports indicate the supervisory board has scheduled a special meeting for August 25 to discuss a potential spin-off of the "Transformation of Industry" division — the steam turbine and compressor business employing around 17,000 people.

The meeting is currently framed as a consultation, not a decision point. That distinction matters for investors. A clear commitment to a spin-off would signal a focused push toward the higher-margin, growth-oriented segments — gas turbines, grid technology, and the now-profitable Gamesa. A delay or rejection would raise questions about whether management intends to stick with the current broad structure.

sum: - Barclays shifted its rating on Siemens Energy from “Equal Weight” to “Underweight,” triggering a 5%+ decline in shares on Tuesday.
- Despite lifting its price target to €130 from €110, the bank cautioned that current valuations assume perpetual peak conditions.
- Sustainable annual demand for global power equipment is estimated at 80–90 GW, about 15% lower than present order levels.
- Peak free cash flow directed to shareholders is anticipated to reach approximately €7.6 billion in fiscal 2026 before tapering off.
- Leading turbine manufacturers have already locked in over 70 GW worth of data center commitments, reducing potential for additional surprises.

Shares of Siemens Energy AG tumbled over 5% on Tuesday following a downgrade to “Underweight” from Barclays, making it the DAX’s biggest laggard during the trading session. The stock hovered around €146 when the downgrade was issued, retreating from year-to-date gains of approximately 35% prior to the announcement.

Barclays analyst Vlad Sergievskii delivered the downgrade while simultaneously lifting the firm’s price target to €130 from €110 — though the revised target still suggests substantial downside from prevailing price levels.
